papers.title: Attribution assignment for deep-generative sequence models enables interpretability analysis using positive-only data.
papers.abstract: Generative machine learning models offer a powerful framework for therapeutic design, by efficiently exploring large spaces of biological sequences enriched for desirable properties. Unlike supervised learning methods, which require both positive and negative labeled data, generative models such as LSTMs can be trained solely on positively labeled sequences, for example, high-affinity antibodies. This is particularly advantageous in biological settings where negative data are scarce, unreliable, or biologically ill-defined. However, the lack of attribution methods for generative models has hin
papers.summary: The authors introduce an attribution method for deep generative sequence models (e.g., LSTMs) trained only on positive examples, enabling interpretability without requiring negative data. This allows researchers to identify which sequence features drive model predictions in therapeutic design tasks like antibody engineering. The work addresses a key gap in explaining generative models when only positive biological sequences are available.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors developed MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrated its utility for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Multitask Framework Integrating Habitat and Deep Learning for Predicting Early Disease Control and Survival in Immunotherapy-Treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients show heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study developed ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask network integrating CT-derived habitat and 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning features for simultaneously predicting early disease control (DC) and overall survival (OS). Of 1,234 patients with HCC enrolled from eight institutions and public databases, 832 ICI-treated patients were used for model development. ECOS-Net fused features using multi-head attention and generated early DC probabilities and OS risk scores. ECOS-DC a
papers.summary: This study introduces ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask deep learning framework that combines CT-derived habitat imaging features with 2.5D deep learning to simultaneously predict early disease control and overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Trained on 832 ICI-treated patients from eight institutions, the model aims to address heterogeneous treatment responses by generating both early DC probabilities and OS risk scores.

papers.title: SpaCEy links spatial tissue patterns to clinical outcomes using explainable graph neural networks.
papers.abstract: Tissues are complex ecosystems organised in space, and alterations in this organisation underpin multiple diseases. Spatial omics enables molecular profiling of tissue organisation, but linking these patterns to clinical outcomes remains challenging. We present SpaCEy (Spatial Clinical Explainability), an explainable graph neural network that identifies tissue patterns predictive of clinical outcomes in spatial proteomics datasets. SpaCEy models tissues as spatial graphs from molecular marker expression, without using predefined cell-type labels or anatomical regions as model inputs. Its embed
papers.summary: SpaCEy is an explainable graph neural network that models spatial proteomics data as graphs built directly from molecular marker expression, avoiding reliance on predefined cell-type labels or anatomical regions. It identifies spatial tissue patterns that predict clinical outcomes and provides interpretability into which patterns drive those predictions. This offers a general framework for connecting tissue organization to patient outcomes in spatial omics studies.

papers.title: Symptom Terminology Normalization in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Development and Evaluation of a 2-Stage Deep Learning Framework Based on Fine-Grained Semantic Classification.
papers.abstract: Due to the heterogeneity of symptom terminology and the lack of industry standards, the same symptom is often described using multiple expressions. Current normalization approaches struggle to comprehensively retrieve standard terms when a raw term maps to multiple symptoms.
papers.summary: This paper develops a two-stage deep learning framework for normalizing symptom terminology in Traditional Chinese Medicine, addressing the problem that the same symptom is often expressed in many different ways. The approach uses fine-grained semantic classification to handle cases where a raw term can map to multiple standard symptoms, and the authors evaluate its performance against existing normalization methods.

papers.title: ASAS-NANP SYMPOSIUM: MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN ANIMAL NUTRITION: The Evolution of Large Language Models and Their Impact on Animal Sciences.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of large language models (LLM) is reshaping the scientific landscape, transitioning from early statistical language models to advanced transformer-based architectures capable of synthesizing knowledge across disciplines. While their predictive capacity and scalability have opened new avenues in data analysis, hypothesis generation, and decision support, concerns remain regarding bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance. In animal sciences, LLM are gradually applied to challenges in nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. Prec
papers.summary: This symposium paper reviews the evolution of large language models from early statistical approaches to modern transformer architectures and discusses their emerging applications in animal sciences, including nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. It also highlights key concerns such as bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance that must be addressed for responsible adoption.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods and global structural alignment tools, which suffer from high false positive rates when proteins share overall structural similarity but differ in catalytic function.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTAC molecules, which are bifunctional compounds that degrade target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, aiming to produce more synthesizable and effective degraders. The work addresses a key bottleneck in PROTAC development: the lack of structure-activity data and the combinatorial complexity of linker chemistry.

papers.title: Learning Protein-Protein Binding Free Energies from Interface Graphs and Physicochemical Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-protein binding free energy (ΔG) from structure remains a central challenge in computational biophysics. Here, we present GULP (Graph-based Unified Learning for Protein binding), a graph neural network (GNN) that jointly learns from a residue-level graph representation of the binding interface and global physicochemical descriptors. We systematically investigate how training data distribution affects model performance by comparing a full training set with a balanced subset enriched for extreme-affinity complexes. GULP is computationally efficient and provides interpretable i
papers.summary: GULP is a graph neural network that predicts protein-protein binding free energy by combining residue-level interface graphs with global physicochemical descriptors. The authors show that training data distribution, particularly enrichment for extreme-affinity complexes, strongly affects performance, and the model is both computationally efficient and interpretable.

papers.title: Portable near-infrared spectroscopy combined with machine learning for rapid detection of broiler breast myopathies.
papers.abstract: Growth-related breast myopathies are among the major meat quality defects encountered in modern broiler production, affecting breast meat quality and requiring affected fillets to be diverted to further processing. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of a pocket-sized near‑infrared (NIR) spectrometer for detecting white striping (WS), wooden breast (WB), and spaghetti meat (SM) in broiler breast meat. A total of 4579 broilers from a commercial crossbred and a broiler breeders line were sampled across 8 flocks and multiple slaughter days, and fillets were categorized by a trained evalu
papers.summary: This study tested whether a pocket-sized near-infrared spectrometer combined with machine learning can detect common broiler breast muscle defects (white striping, wooden breast, and spaghetti meat) in chicken fillets. Using 4,579 broilers across multiple flocks and slaughter days, the authors found that the portable NIR approach could rapidly classify affected meat, offering a potential on-line quality screening tool for poultry processing.

papers.title: Integrated Systems Toxicology Analysis and Molecular Dynamics Study Reveal the Potential Mechanism by which Benzo[a]pyrene Contributes to Depression in Lung Adenocarcinoma via RNASE1 Upregulation.
papers.abstract: Benzo-[a]-pyrene (Bap), a prominent carcinogen found in tobacco smoke and air pollution, is closely associated with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and subsequent depression, though the mechanism underlying this comorbidity remains unclear. LUAD patients were categorized based on depression-related gene expression. Prognostic genes identified through machine learning were cross-referenced with predicted Bap targets. Mendelian randomization (MR) evaluated the causal relationship between RNASE1 and depression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (M
papers.summary: This study integrates systems toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular dynamics to uncover how benzo[a]pyrene exposure may drive depression in lung adenocarcinoma patients through upregulation of RNASE1. The findings suggest RNASE1 as a potential mechanistic link and therapeutic target connecting environmental carcinogen exposure, LUAD, and comorbid depression.

papers.title: Chemically Informed Machine Learning Approach for Prediction of Reactivity Ratios in Radical Copolymerization.
papers.abstract: Predicting monomer reactivity ratios is crucial for controlling monomer sequence distribution in copolymers and their properties. Traditional experimental methods of determining reactivity ratios are time-consuming and resource-intensive, while existing computational methods often struggle with accuracy or scalability. Here, we present a method that combines unsupervised learning with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. By applying spectral clustering to physicochemical features of monomers, we identified three distinct monomer groups with chara
papers.summary: The paper introduces a machine learning method that combines spectral clustering of monomer physicochemical features with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. This approach aims to overcome the time and resource demands of experimental determination and the accuracy/scalability limitations of existing computational methods.

papers.title: HD-AIP: A Heterogeneous Dual-Stream Alignment-Free Framework for Anti-Inflammatory Peptide Prediction Based on Language Models and CT-Net.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) show therapeutic potential for treating chronic and autoimmune diseases. Computational screening of these peptides remains challenging because their typically short sequences limit traditional feature extraction effectiveness, while homology-based methods incur high computational costs.
papers.summary: The authors present HD-AIP, an alignment-free computational framework that combines protein language models with a CT-Net architecture in a dual-stream design to predict anti-inflammatory peptides. The approach targets the difficulty of screening short peptide sequences, where traditional feature extraction and homology-based methods struggle with limited information and high computational cost.

papers.title: BiMSGP: A Bidirectional Mamba-Based Model for Scalable and Accurate Genomic Prediction in Plants.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate prediction of complex traits from high-dimensional genomic markers remains difficult in plant breeding. Linear models have limited capacity for non-linear interactions, and many deep learning models scale poorly on long marker sequences. This study introduces BiMSGP, a bidirectional Mamba-based model for scalable genomic prediction. Methods: BiMSGP extends a selective state space model with forward and backward processing so that each marker can integrate sequence context from both directions while retaining linear computational complexity; this is a modeling de
papers.summary: BiMSGP is a deep learning model for genomic prediction in plant breeding that uses a bidirectional Mamba architecture to capture non-linear interactions between genetic markers while maintaining linear computational complexity. It processes marker sequences in both forward and backward directions, enabling each marker to incorporate context from both sides, addressing scalability issues of prior deep learning models on long marker sequences.

papers.title: Combined Analysis of Transcriptome and Metabolome of Large-Size Triploid Rainbow Trout in Different Seasons.
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variation poses a significant physiological challenge for cold-water aquaculture species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying seasonal adaptation in large-sized triploid rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated liver transcriptomics and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics across four seasons (February, May, August, November) to investigate this phenomenon. Seasonal comparisons revealed pronounced molecular reprogramming, with the comparison between May and August showing the largest transcriptomic shift (13,359 di
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrated liver transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics in large triploid rainbow trout across four seasons to understand seasonal adaptation. The largest molecular shift occurred between May and August, revealing extensive transcriptomic and metabolic reprogramming linked to temperature changes. The findings provide molecular insights that could inform cold-water aquaculture management.

papers.title: CDELDA: A Content-Based Dual-Encoder for Cold-Start lncRNA-Disease Association Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: An important challenge in long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)-disease association prediction is prioritizing candidates when neither target node has association records in the training data, even though content features are available. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a content-based model for this both-cold setting. Methods: We developed CDELDA, a dual-encoder model combining lncRNA sequence, structure, and expression features with disease text, semantic similarity, and ontology-structure features. CDELDA was compared with five baseline methods on a normalized benchmark
papers.summary: CDELDA is a dual-encoder model that predicts lncRNA-disease associations in the challenging 'both-cold' setting, where neither the lncRNA nor the disease has any prior association records in the training data. It combines lncRNA sequence, structure, and expression features with disease text, semantic similarity, and ontology features, and was benchmarked against five baseline methods.

papers.title: A reference genome without a virus: cDNA reconstruction reveals the provenance and function of the MS2 phage sequence.
papers.abstract: Reference genomes are often treated as faithful representations of experimentally validated viral genomes, yet the relationship between historically curated reference sequences and infectivity is rarely tested experimentally. Here, we developed a cDNA-based reconstruction platform for the canonical RNA phage MS2 and used it to compare the current NCBI reference genome (RefSeq) with closely related published isolate sequences. We found that isolate-derived sequences reproducibly yielded infectious phage, whereas the current MS2 RefSeq-derived construct did not, showing that the present referenc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a cDNA-based reverse genetics platform for the RNA phage MS2 and found that the current NCBI RefSeq reference genome does not produce infectious phage, while closely related published isolate sequences do. This shows that the curated reference sequence has diverged from functional, infectious MS2 and that reference genomes should not be assumed to be experimentally validated.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based machine learning model that predicts how mutations change protein thermal stability, classifying changes into multiple categories rather than just binary stable/unstable. Unlike prior methods that encode reference and mutant sequences separately, it explicitly models the mutation context, and the authors apply it to the enzyme CcsZ. This offers a faster, cheaper alternative to experimental screening of large mutational libraries for protein engineering.

papers.title: Mapping Gene Expression to an Interpretable Semantic Space.
papers.abstract: Cell embeddings organize single-cell expression data, but their dimensions have no biological meaning, so clusters are interpreted afterward. We present MESIC (Mapping Expression to Semantic space with Interpretable Components), which builds the written knowledge about genes held in curated databases into the dimensions themselves. A biomedical language model converts each gene's summary into a semantic embedding. MESIC compresses these embeddings into a small number of components, each concentrated on a small set of genes and explained by their annotations. The components are computed once fr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MESIC is a new method that builds interpretable dimensions for single-cell expression data by using a biomedical language model to convert curated gene summaries into semantic embeddings, then compressing them into components concentrated on small gene sets. This allows cell embeddings to have direct biological meaning from the start, rather than requiring post-hoc interpretation of clusters.

papers.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
papers.abstract: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral
papers.summary: The authors present VirPLM, a fine-tuned protein language model for predicting antigenic relationships between influenza A/H3N2 strains directly from hemagglutinin HA1 sequences. This offers a scalable, sequence-based alternative to labor-intensive hemagglutination inhibition assays, which are the current gold standard for antigenic characterization. The approach leverages the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences to support more timely vaccine strain selection.

papers.title: Regulatory-prior-guided attention preserves biological structure during unpaired single-cell RNA-ATAC integration.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing provide complementary views of transcriptional output and chromatin regulatory potential, but integrating unpaired profiles remains challenging because the modalities differ in feature space, sparsity and noise. Existing approaches often frame integration as distribution matching, which can over-align biologically distinct, condition-specific or modality-specific cell states. We present scHPGT, a single-cell Heterogeneous Prior-Guided Transformer for regulatory-prior-guided integration of unpaired RNA and chromatin accessibility profil
papers.summary: The authors present scHPGT, a transformer-based method that integrates unpaired single-cell RNA and ATAC profiles by incorporating regulatory priors rather than relying purely on distribution matching. This prior-guided attention mechanism helps preserve biologically meaningful structure, avoiding the over-alignment of distinct cell states that can occur with conventional integration approaches.

papers.title: Bridging Nano-Interface Interactions and Organ-Specific Toxicity: A Review of Machine Learning for Nanomaterials Risk Assessment.
papers.abstract: Risk assessment of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) is essential for protecting human health and the environment. Traditional hazard assessments rely primarily on in vivo testing, which faces technical challenges in extrapolation validity, ethical dilemmas, and high costs. Machine learning (ML) models offer alternative approaches that are aligned with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement) for reducing animal use. ML methods help address the economic, ethical, and temporal limitations of traditional nanotoxicology while advancing mechanistic understanding. This review presen
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning approaches for predicting the toxicity of engineered nanomaterials, aiming to reduce reliance on animal testing in line with 3R principles. It connects nano-interface interactions to organ-specific toxicity outcomes and discusses how ML can advance mechanistic understanding while addressing cost and ethical limitations of traditional nanotoxicology.

papers.title: HERA: Bioinspired Separation of Local Fault Response and Language-Model Scheduling in Simulated Quadruped Control.
papers.abstract: Language-model inference can delay emergency supervision, but cancellation alone cannot provide an immediate physical response. HERA (Hierarchical Event-driven Reflex Architecture) separates a measurement-driven deterministic local action from language-service scheduling, with biological inspiration limited to temporal separation and local feedback. A fixed 1472-trial campaign evaluated canonical-command scheduling, simulated actuator faults and live integration. Across three workloads, the mean validated-command latency was 0.486-0.512 s with preemption, 1.476-11.101 s with single-lane FIFO a
papers.summary: HERA is a control architecture for simulated quadruped robots that separates fast, deterministic local reflex responses from slower language-model-based scheduling, inspired by biological temporal separation. In a 1472-trial campaign, preemptive scheduling reduced validated-command latency to roughly 0.5 seconds versus 1.5–11 seconds with single-lane FIFO, while still handling simulated actuator faults. The work shows that decoupling local fault response from LLM inference can improve emergency responsiveness in robot control.

papers.title: 3D Spatial Interactomics Maps the Dynamics of NF-κB Multiprotein Signalosomes in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: NFκB signaling drives inflammatory responses by rapidly assembling membrane-proximal multiprotein supercomplexes, yet how these assemblies are organized in space and time within the 3D interior of a single cell has remained uncharacterized. We addressed this by profiling endogenous NFκB protein-protein interactions with an intelligent sequential proximity ligation assay (iseqPLA), read out by spinning disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. Each detected protein-protein proximity event is represented by a rolling-circle amplification product, and we treat clusters of co-localized punct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces iseqPLA, a sequential proximity ligation assay combined with spinning-disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction, to map endogenous NF-κB protein-protein interactions in single cells. The method reveals how membrane-proximal NF-κB multiprotein signalosomes assemble dynamically in 3D space and time, with each interaction event visualized as a rolling-circle amplification punct. It provides a new way to study spatial interactomics of signaling complexes at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology.
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, human aging has been characterized across DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical modalities, yet no benchmark evaluates whether AI systems can interpret these heterogeneous data types in the context of aging biology. We introduce LongevityBench, an open suite of 17 tasks spanning five biodata domains, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI systems from six developer teams. Despite recent advances in AI, no single model dominates all tasks, with omics-based age prediction being the hardest task regardless of scale. To test whether these gaps can be clos
papers.summary: The authors introduce LongevityBench, an open benchmark of 17 tasks across five biodata domains designed to evaluate how well AI systems can interpret aging-related data. Testing 18 frontier AI models, they find that no single model excels across all tasks, and omics-based age prediction remains the hardest challenge regardless of model scale.

papers.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cell Types in Describing Neuronal Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) captures detailed gene expression profiles at scale, while patch-clamp recordings measure intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties. Modeling the relations between these two modalities remains a challenge. Here, we compare how well electrophysiological features can be predicted by traditional transcriptomic cell type classification, representations derived from a foundational model (scGPT) pretrained on large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, ion channel-coding genes, and highly variable genes. Using paired transcriptomic and electrophysiological patch-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares how well different transcriptomic representations predict neuronal electrophysiological properties from paired patch-clamp and scRNA-seq data. Traditional cell type classifications outperform scGPT foundational model embeddings, ion channel-coding genes, and highly variable genes in predicting physiological features. The results suggest that cell type identity remains a remarkably strong and simple descriptor of neuronal physiology.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover functional modules and provide phenotype-informed biological annotations. It aims to overcome the interpretability limitations of existing module discovery and pathway-based methods by producing coherent, non-redundant functional insights. The tool is designed to help researchers translate complex molecular signatures into biologically meaningful mechanisms.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information to predict and interpret protein function, while also supporting natural language interaction. It addresses the gap between models that handle either natural language or genomic code by fusing both modalities, aiming to make DNA-encoded function more human-readable and useful for disease and drug research.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a deep learning method that predicts whether a DNA-binding protein binds single-stranded or double-stranded DNA. It combines a bilinear convolutional attention network with an adaptive sampling strategy to handle class imbalance and improve prediction accuracy. The approach aims to support drug discovery and functional annotation of DNA-binding proteins.

papers.title: miRAssist: a context-aware, evidence integration framework for interpretable miRNA-target prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNA-target interaction prediction remains challenging because many existing tools provide prediction scores or ranked candidate lists without making the supporting evidence easy to interpret or relate to a specific biological context.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: miRAssist is a new computational framework that predicts microRNA-target interactions while integrating multiple lines of supporting evidence and making the reasoning behind each prediction interpretable. Unlike existing tools that output opaque scores or ranked lists, it provides context-aware, evidence-linked prioritization to help researchers understand why a given miRNA-target pair is predicted.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: The authors propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework for predicting drug-target binding affinity in Ebola, a disease with scarce experimental affinity data. The method leverages the large BindingDB interaction dataset, using compound- and protein-similarity retrieval to select the most relevant source interactions for transfer to the Ebola target domain. This two-stage strategy aims to improve DTA prediction accuracy in low-resource settings.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Identify Immune-Linked Gene Signatures for LUAD Stratification.
papers.abstract: Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common subtype of non-small-cell lung cancer and is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally. Despite current developments, reliable biomarkers for effective diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification are still lacking. Methods: We analyzed publicly available TCGA-LUAD and GEO datasets using integrative bioinformatics approaches, including differential gene expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), survival modeling, mutation profiling, immune cell infiltration scores, machine learning, and bulk
papers.summary: This study integrates TCGA-LUAD and GEO transcriptomic data with WGCNA, survival modeling, mutation profiling, and immune infiltration analysis to identify immune-linked gene signatures that stratify lung adenocarcinoma patients. Machine learning approaches were used to refine and validate these signatures, potentially improving prognosis and patient stratification. The work highlights immune-related biomarkers as promising tools for LUAD diagnosis and risk assessment.

papers.title: Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Bacteriophage Research: A New Chapter in Future Medicine.
papers.abstract: As the crisis of antibiotic resistance escalates, phage therapy has regained attention as an alternative strategy. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer new avenues to overcome the bottlenecks inherent in traditional bacteriophage research. This review summarizes the multi-dimensional innovative applications of machine learning, deep learning, and large biological models in phage studies. In the fields of phage recognition and genomics, support vector machines (SVMs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and pre-trained protein language models can all achieve recognition accuracy ra
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning, deep learning, and large biological language models are being applied across bacteriophage research, including phage recognition, genomics, and therapeutic development. It highlights that methods like SVMs, CNNs, and pre-trained protein language models can achieve high accuracy in tasks such as phage identification, positioning AI as a tool to accelerate phage therapy amid rising antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Routine Laboratory-Based Machine Learning for Discriminating Multiple Myeloma from Clinical Mimickers: Development and Internal Validation of a Diagnostic Prediction Model.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple myeloma (MM) diagnosis requires specialised testing that is not universally available, contributing to diagnostic delays. The aim of this study was to develop and internally validate statistical and machine learning (ML) models that discriminate MM from clinically similar conditions using exclusively routine laboratory parameters. Methods: This retrospective diagnostic prediction model study included 422 consecutive patients referred to hematology for suspected MM at a tertiary care center (2017-2025). Fifteen routine demographic and laboratory variables were used to train
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated machine learning models that distinguish multiple myeloma from clinically similar conditions using only routine demographic and laboratory variables, avoiding specialized testing. Using data from 422 patients referred for suspected myeloma, the models aim to reduce diagnostic delays in settings where advanced testing is unavailable.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict inhibitors of coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa), using IC50 data from ChEMBL and scaffold-aware validation. Ensemble methods were applied to build models that balance predictive accuracy with interpretability, aiding drug discovery for contact-system-related targets.

papers.title: Biopesticidal Potential of the Cannabis sativa L. Metabolites: A Denoised, Docking-Informed QSAR Model.
papers.abstract: Plant metabolites are a promising source of new biopesticides, but their chemical diversity exceeds the capacity of experimental screening. Cannabis sativa is a particularly attractive crop for discovering such compounds, although its metabolome has not been systematically evaluated for biopesticidal potential. Here, we computationally analyzed 5211 compounds annotated as C. sativa metabolites in the Cannabis Compound Database (CCD) using an integrated framework combining graph-based molecular prediction and protein-ligand interaction analysis. Initial prioritization employed a directed messag
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 5,211 Cannabis sativa metabolites from the Cannabis Compound Database for biopesticidal potential using a docking-informed QSAR framework that combines graph-based molecular prediction with protein-ligand interaction analysis. The authors developed a denoised model to prioritize compounds, demonstrating a scalable approach to mine plant metabolomes for new biopesticides without exhaustive experimental screening.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Guided Identification and In Vivo Validation of Compact Cis-Regulatory Elements for the Zebrafish Habenula.
papers.abstract: Precise genetic access to the zebrafish habenula remains limited by a scarcity of compact, sequence-defined cis-regulatory elements (CREs). Here, we integrated developmental expression mapping, deep-learning predictions on long-range sequences, and in vivo reporter assays to identify compact regulatory sequences driving habenular expression.
papers.summary: This study combines developmental expression mapping with deep-learning predictions to identify compact cis-regulatory elements (CREs) that drive gene expression specifically in the zebrafish habenula, a brain region important for emotional and cognitive processing. The predicted CREs were validated in vivo using reporter assays, providing new genetic tools for targeting this brain region. The work demonstrates how deep learning can guide the discovery of functional regulatory sequences in a vertebrate model.

papers.title: From Machine Learning-Enhanced Proteomics to a Validated Diagnostic Model: A Pipeline for Breast Cancer Biomarker Discovery via Independent and Transcriptomic Corroboration.
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis of breast cancer (BC) remains challenging. The limited sensitivity and specificity of existing serum tumor markers for reliable clinical application highlight the need to develop a more accurate and efficient screening workflow. This study analyzed serum samples from 255 breast cancer patients and 300 healthy controls using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry, identifying 58 differentially expressed peptides (37 upregulated, 21 downregulated). Combined with machine learning, peptide identification, and external validation, a
papers.summary: This study used MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry to profile serum peptides from 255 breast cancer patients and 300 healthy controls, identifying 58 differentially expressed peptides. By integrating machine learning with peptide identification and external validation, the authors built a diagnostic model for breast cancer that was corroborated by independent and transcriptomic data. The work presents a pipeline for serum-based biomarker discovery aimed at improving early breast cancer detection.

papers.title: A Robust Masked Painter Framework for Gene Selection in Binary Classification of High-Dimensional Functional Genomic Data.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional gene expression datasets in chemometric and biomedical research present significant challenges for machine learning because the number of genes greatly exceeds the number of available samples, increasing the risk of overfitting and reducing classification reliability. Existing gene selection methods are often sensitive to noise and outliers, leading to unstable feature subsets and degraded classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework that integrates robust measures of location and dispersion, namely the M
papers.summary: This paper introduces the Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework, a gene selection method designed to handle high-dimensional gene expression data where the number of genes far exceeds the number of samples. By incorporating robust statistical measures of location and dispersion, the method aims to reduce sensitivity to noise and outliers, leading to more stable feature subsets and improved binary classification performance.

papers.title: Evaluating Sequence Foundation Models for Insect Olfactory Gene Discovery: Failure Modes, Evidence Standards, and a Benchmark Agenda.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale searches for insect olfactory genes are vulnerable to rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage between training and test data. Sequence foundation models trained on DNA or proteins may extend homology-based annotation, but available evidence does not support their use as autonomous annotators or direct predictors of sensory function. This critical review organizes the problem around annotation failures rather than model catalogues. We distinguish six inference levels, from candidate locus detection to organism
papers.summary: This critical review examines whether sequence foundation models can reliably identify insect olfactory genes, arguing that current evidence does not support their use as autonomous annotators or direct predictors of sensory function. It organizes the problem around six inference levels and highlights failure modes such as rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage. The authors propose a benchmark agenda and evidence standards to guide future work.

papers.title: A Systematic Machine Learning Framework for Evaluating and Ranking Omics Layers in Cancer Drug Response Prediction.
papers.abstract: This study introduces a top-down framework for evaluating the utility of multi-omics features to predict the response of 309 drugs in cancer cell lines. This was done by taking a multi-omics approach where data from proteomic, transcriptomic, genomic, metabolomic, and miRNA were integrated with drug sensitivity (area under the curve, AUC) data. We performed modular dimensionality reduction using t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding), followed by K-Means clustering to stratify cell lines into data-driven molecular subgroups, and applied a Random Forest model to refine the drug lis
papers.summary: This study builds a machine learning framework to test how well different omics layers (proteomics, transcriptomics, genomics, metabolomics, miRNA) predict cancer drug response across 309 drugs in cell lines. Using t-SNE dimensionality reduction, K-Means clustering, and Random Forest models, the authors rank which omics data types are most informative for drug response prediction. The work provides a systematic comparison of omics layers, helping prioritize data types for future pharmacogenomic modeling.

papers.title: Identification of key genes and mechanistic exploration of metabolic reprogramming in osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo identify metabolism-related genes associated with osteoporosis and evaluate their diagnostic potential through integrative transcriptomic analysis and clinical validation.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE169396 were analyzed using the Seurat package to investigate interactions between monocytes and other cell types. Metabolic pathway alterations in osteoporosis were evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. Differentially expressed genes were intersected with metabolism-related genes to identify differentially expressed metabolism-related genes. Key
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic data to identify metabolism-related genes associated with osteoporosis, focusing on monocyte interactions and metabolic pathway alterations. The authors pinpoint candidate diagnostic genes through differential expression analysis and clinical validation. The work highlights metabolic reprogramming as a potential contributor to osteoporosis pathogenesis and proposes candidate biomarkers.

papers.title: Pathogen genome enrichment sequencing to support a city-wide Legionnaires' disease outbreak investigation.
papers.abstract: Pathogen genomics can provide high-confidence source attribution for epidemiological investigations of Legionnaires' disease (LD) outbreaks. However, the utility of culture-based genomics can be undermined by long lead times for Legionella pneumophila culture or a lack of isolates when dealing with non-culturable bacteria or low-biomass specimens. Here, during a large 2024 LD outbreak in Melbourne, Australia, we compared direct specimen, hybridization-based enrichment sequencing with traditional culture-based whole-genome sequencing of 18 clinical and 5 environmental L. pneumophila specimens.
papers.summary: During a 2024 Legionnaires' disease outbreak in Melbourne, researchers compared direct hybridization-based enrichment sequencing of clinical and environmental specimens against traditional culture-based whole-genome sequencing of Legionella pneumophila. The enrichment approach enabled genomic analysis without the delays and culturing limitations of conventional methods, supporting faster outbreak source attribution.

papers.title: A cfDNA-based DNA methylation classifier for distinguishing prostate cancer from benign prostatic hyperplasia.
papers.abstract: Differentiating benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) from prostate cancer (PCa) remains a diagnostic challenge due to overlapping clinical features and the limited specificity of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing. Recent studies highlight the promise of DNA methylation patterns in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as non-invasive biomarkers for prostate disease stratification. This study aimed to develop a targeted methylation-based diagnostic model capable of distinguishing PCa from BPH using cfDNA. We hypothesized that specific genomic regions exhibit consistent hyper- or hypomethylation signatures
papers.summary: This study develops a targeted DNA methylation classifier using cell-free DNA (cfDNA) to distinguish prostate cancer from benign prostatic hyperplasia, addressing the poor specificity of PSA testing. By identifying genomic regions with consistent hyper- or hypomethylation signatures in cfDNA, the authors aim to provide a non-invasive diagnostic tool for prostate disease stratification.

papers.title: Cross-Model Uncertainty-Aware Minimal Editing of Cis-Regulatory Elements for Cell-Type-Selective Design.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cis-regulatory elements (CREs) help mediate cell-type-selective gene expression, yet sequence-to-activity models are rarely converted into compact, experimentally tractable variant panels that retain natural regulatory scaffolds. We developed SafeEdit-CRE to select minimal edits that preserve cross-model specificity while reducing predictive uncertainty, yielding an auditable CRE variant library for reporter-screening prioritization. Methods: SafeEdit-CRE combines the published Malinois sequence-activity predictor with an architecture-distinct reviewer ensemble, validati
papers.summary: SafeEdit-CRE is a computational framework that designs minimal edits to cis-regulatory elements (CREs) to achieve cell-type-selective gene expression while preserving natural regulatory scaffolds. It combines the Malinois sequence-activity predictor with an architecture-distinct reviewer ensemble to reduce predictive uncertainty and produce an auditable variant library for reporter-screening prioritization.

papers.title: Integrating Plant-Based Coagulation and Explainable Machine Learning for Sustainable River Water Treatment.
papers.abstract: Industrial wastewater discharge has severely degraded freshwater resources, necessitating the development of sustainable and environmentally benign treatment technologies. This study investigates the performance of three plant-based natural coagulants, namely, Moringa leaf powder (MLP), banana peel powder (BPP), and neem leaf powder (NLP), for the treatment of Sirsa River water contaminated with organic pollutants and heavy metals. Coagulation-flocculation experiments were conducted under optimized operating conditions, and treatment efficiency was evaluated based on turbidity, chemical oxygen
papers.journal: Water environment research : a research publication of the Water Environment Federation
papers.summary: This study evaluates three plant-based natural coagulants (Moringa leaf, banana peel, and neem leaf powders) for treating contaminated river water, optimizing coagulation-flocculation conditions to reduce turbidity and pollutants. The authors integrate explainable machine learning to interpret and predict treatment performance, aiming to support sustainable, low-cost water treatment. The work demonstrates a green alternative to conventional chemical coagulants with interpretable predictive modeling.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The authors report elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells from RPL patients, suggesting specific immune dysregulations that may disrupt maternal-fetal tolerance in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: FatPlants 2.0: an AI-powered platform integrating plant lipid genes, pathways, and literature.
papers.abstract: Plant lipid research depends on accessible databases that connect genes, pathways, and prior literature. However, currently available resources are fragmented, species-limited, and lack AI-powered interfaces for integrated querying. FatPlants 2.0 addresses these issues by integrating ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental data into a unified platform with 14 000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways across 5 species, and 57 000+ curated publications. The platform features LipidBot, an AI agent enabling natural language queries via graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented ge
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: FatPlants 2.0 is an updated plant lipid database that unifies ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress data into a single platform covering 14,000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways, and 57,000+ publications across five species. It introduces LipidBot, an AI agent that lets researchers query genes, pathways, and literature using natural language. The platform aims to overcome fragmentation and limited species coverage in existing plant lipid resources.

papers.title: PhoSARte: identification of SARS-CoV-2 phosphorylation sites using contrastive learning and protein language models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation, a critical post-translational modification, is extensively altered during viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, where it plays a central role in modulating host-pathogen interactions. Accurately identifying these specific phosphorylation sites is crucial for understanding viral pathogenesis, prioritizing antiviral targets, guiding therapeutic strategies, and strengthening preparedness for future viral outbreaks. Although several computational tools have been proposed to complement experimental phosphoproteomics, existing methods often show limited robustness, cross-viral gen
papers.summary: PhoSARte is a computational tool that uses contrastive learning combined with protein language models to predict phosphorylation sites specifically in SARS-CoV-2 proteins. It aims to improve on existing phosphoproteomics prediction methods, which often lack robustness and generalize poorly across viral genomes. The tool is intended to help identify host-pathogen interaction points and prioritize antiviral drug targets.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The authors present a structure-based deep learning framework that combines a graph transformer with a pretrained protein language model to classify bacterial virulence factors into functional classes. By incorporating spatial structure information alongside sequence data, the method aims to improve prediction of virulence factor categories, which could aid in understanding bacterial pathogenesis and identifying antivirulence targets.

papers.title: Developing SCL2205: a protein sequence-based spatial modelling dataset for the protein language model frontier.
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has substantially advanced protein subcellular localization (SCL) prediction, yet its potential remains constrained by suboptimal input preparation and limited high-quality reference data. Furthermore, existing state-of-the-art (SoTA) predictors suffer from performance metric inflation due to unmitigated training-to-testing data leakage during homology augmentation. We address these challenges by introducing SCL2205, a leak-minimized benchmark dataset and pipeline curated specifically to support trustworthy, scalable, and reproducible DL-based SCL modelling.
papers.summary: The authors introduce SCL2205, a curated benchmark dataset and pipeline for predicting protein subcellular localization using deep learning. The dataset is specifically designed to minimize data leakage from homology-based augmentation, which has inflated performance metrics in existing state-of-the-art predictors. This provides a more trustworthy and reproducible foundation for evaluating protein language models on spatial localization tasks.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic profiles of tolerogenic dendritic cells with keloid transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDCs to keloid pathology. The authors identify key tolDC-associated genes and perform preliminary mRNA validation, suggesting these genes may contribute to keloid immunopathology. The findings highlight a potential role for tolDCs in keloid formation and provide candidate targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Genetic Analyses Identify CDC20 as a Potential Biomarker Associated with Cell Cycle and Immune-Inflammatory Processes in Psoriasis.
papers.abstract: To identify psoriasis-associated candidate genes and regulatory features via integrated transcriptomic, immune and genetic analyses, and validate them in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like murine model.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic, immune, and genetic analyses to identify CDC20 as a candidate biomarker for psoriasis, linking it to cell cycle regulation and immune-inflammatory processes. The findings were validated in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, supporting CDC20 as a potential diagnostic or therapeutic target.

papers.title: Metal- and polymer-assisted SEM imaging of protein-bound DNA molecules: a protocol.
papers.abstract: Direct mapping of protein positions along long, stretched DNA molecules requires simultaneous visualization of the DNA backbone and associated protein signals. We recently established a heavy-metal- and polymer-assisted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) approach for imaging stretched DNA molecules and associated protein signals on silicon wafers. Here, we present a practical protocol for implementing this workflow using λ DNA and streptavidin-fluorescent protein-labeled λ DNA as model DNA samples. The protocol encompasses silicon wafer preparation, microchannel-guided DNA deposition, heavy-me
papers.summary: This protocol describes a heavy-metal- and polymer-assisted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) method for visualizing stretched DNA molecules and the positions of bound proteins on silicon wafers. Using λ DNA and streptavidin-fluorescent protein-labeled λ DNA as models, it provides step-by-step guidance covering wafer preparation, microchannel-guided DNA deposition, and metal staining. The approach enables direct mapping of protein binding sites along long DNA molecules at high resolution.

papers.title: AI-driven genotype-phenotype modeling: a framework integrating multi-modal single-cell genomics and reverse vaccinology for de novo design of multi-epitope cancer vaccines.
papers.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising strategy for personalized cancer immunotherapy; however, their development has traditionally relied on bulk sequencing approaches that average molecular information across millions of cells, thereby obscuring the extensive intratumoral heterogeneity that drives disease progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune escape. Recent advances in multi-modal single-cell genomics have transformed the ability to characterize tumors at unprecedented resolution, enabling the identification of distinct cellular populations, clonal evolutionary trajectories, a
papers.summary: This paper proposes a computational framework that combines multi-modal single-cell genomics with reverse vaccinology to model genotype-phenotype relationships and design multi-epitope cancer vaccines de novo. It argues that single-cell resolution can capture intratumoral heterogeneity that bulk sequencing misses, potentially improving personalized vaccine target selection. The work is a conceptual/methodological framework rather than an experimentally validated vaccine.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The analysis suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: The paper introduces scLTF, a self-training clustering framework that combines a fast Louvain algorithm with a Transformer model to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets. It aims to overcome performance bottlenecks in existing clustering methods by using preliminary Louvain clusters to guide Transformer-based refinement. The approach is designed to improve clustering accuracy and scalability for large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Architectural good practices for reproducible benchmarking in protein machine learning.
papers.abstract: Reliable benchmarking in protein machine learning requires biological tasks, datasets, representations, execution conditions, and evaluation regimes to be explicitly defined and traceable. Protein-specific dependencies, including label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and potential pretraining contamination, can alter benchmark interpretation. This Perspective provides an operational, protein-specific synthesis of established reproducibility practices through an artefact-linked ar
papers.summary: This perspective article synthesizes reproducibility best practices specifically for benchmarking in protein machine learning, emphasizing that biological tasks, datasets, representations, and evaluation regimes must be explicitly defined and traceable. It highlights protein-specific pitfalls such as label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and pretraining contamination that can distort benchmark interpretation.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. Here, we present a simple generative approach for creating synthetic 5'-UTR libraries based solely on the genomic sequence statistics of any desired organism. T
papers.summary: The authors present a generative language model that creates synthetic 5'-UTR sequence libraries using only the genomic sequence statistics of a target organism, without requiring prior mechanistic knowledge or validated genetic parts. This approach offers a potentially organism-agnostic way to tune translation rates in non-model organisms by modulating upstream untranslated regions.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a conditional protein language model that produces sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers, using molecular dynamics simulations. The generated sequences show high structural stability in simulation, suggesting that language model outputs can yield biologically plausible and stable enzymes.
